samples.summary: Controls carried in `usedControls` across a key bump become invisible in the brief: suppressed from NEVER TRIED but present in no other section
samples.evidence: After a bump, `mergeCoverage` drops the `control|shape` entries (line 317-329, gated on `usable`) but keeps `usedControls` (line 401). `renderCoverageBrief` then subtracts those names from `untried` (line 496) while the ROUND-TRIPPED / applied-but-never-reversed lists are built only from `shapes` (lines 445-446). A control that was clicked before the bump therefore appears in NO section of the brief at all: the explorer is steered away from it (not offered as untried) yet is told nothing about what was already done with it. Before this change it at least appeared under NEVER TRIED (noisily but visibly). This is a behaviour change with a real downside, not only the upside the comment describes.

samples.summary: `usedControls` carries no per-entry sha, so it can never go stale — contradicting the file's own "staleness is per entry" invariant
samples.evidence: Every other memory (`shapes`, `pairs`, `readAfterMutation`, `inventory`) stores `{value, sha}` so `stale()` (line 442) can warn that the tree has moved. `usedControls` is a bare string list (line 286, 401). A control clicked once forty commits ago permanently suppresses itself from NEVER TRIED with no staleness marker, which is exactly the under-warning failure mode the header comment (lines 36-42) says costs a missed defect. It also grows monotonically and is never pruned when a control disappears from the inventory.

samples.summary: `untried` matches used controls by NAME only, ignoring role — a `menuitem` sharing a name with a clicked `button` is silently marked tried
samples.evidence: `inventory` is deliberately keyed on `role|name` (unionInventory, line 355, with the comment at 383-386 saying a menuitem and a button can legitimately share a name), but `untried = inventory.filter((x) => !usedControls.has(x.control))` at line 496 compares names only, and `usedControls` (now also the cross-bump list, which has no role at all) cannot distinguish them. Clicking the `button` "Bold" removes the `menuitem` "Bold" from NEVER TRIED. The pre-existing shapes-derived path had the same hole, but the new cross-bump list makes it permanent and role-less by construction.

samples.summary: `usedControls` bypasses the key-version gate and the loader's "normalise, do not trust" contract keeps only a type filter on arbitrary file content
samples.evidence: Unlike `shapes`/`pairs`/`readAfterMutation` which read the gated `a`/`b`, `usedControls` reads raw `prev`/`next` (lines 403-406), so a coverage.json with any `keyVersion` (including a FUTURE one, where `usable()` is false) contributes names. hunt-ui.mjs:1166 runs hand-editable file content through `mergeCoverage(null, record)` claiming it yields "either valid coverage or empty coverage"; for this field the only validation is `typeof n === "string" && n !== ""` — unbounded length/count, and the strings are interpolated into the explorer prompt via the untried subtraction. Inventory has the same property, so this is an extension of an existing pattern rather than a new class of bug.

samples.summary: `usedControls` sorted with default `.sort()` while every sibling list uses `localeCompare`, so orderings can disagree
samples.evidence: Lines 286 and 408 use bare `.sort()` (UTF-16 code-unit order); `shapes`, `pairs`, `readAfterMutation` and `inventory` all sort via `localeCompare`. With non-ASCII control names the two orders differ, producing gratuitous diff churn in the persisted coverage.json.
